summary:
WEEK ONE WRAP-UP

The division got underway on Saturday with a remarkable spread of opening day results. New Mills made the biggest statement with a stunning 6-0 demolition of Telford Town at Church Lane, with Solomon Richards among the goalscorers. Wolverhampton Casuals also started strongly, winning 3-0 away at newly promoted Crewe, courtesy of goals from Kieran Cook twice and Jake Pearson. Stafford Town edged out Barnton 2-1 in a tighter contest, with Sam Lynch's second-half volley proving decisive after Ben Mooney had equalised for the hosts.

Sandbach United's midweek clash with Wednesfield Community finished 2-1 in their favour, a result that came after Sandbach took the lead early through Bevan's header, saw Wednesfield equalise with what their own posts described as a "freak" deflection, before Bevan notched the winner late on. Joe Bevan continues to rack up the goals — his brace in that game added to his record as Sandbach's all-time leading scorer, now at 58 goals across two seasons.

Elsewhere, AFC Bridgnorth won 3-1 at home to Foley Meir with goals from Sam Preece and Suar (twice), while Bilston Town opened with a 2-0 victory over Shawbury United courtesy of Harry Dixon and Jordan Crump. Eccleshall won 3-1 away at Widnes Town with efforts from Will Silvester, Nicky Parker and Essa Faburay. Brereton Social made an impressive start to their first ever NWCFL campaign, winning 2-0 away at Market Drayton, with Conor Phillips scoring one described as a "goal of the season contender" from distance.

The draws deserve mention too. Cheadle Heath Nomads drew 2-2 at home against Allscott Heath in both sides' opening games. Alsager Town and Dawley Town also drew 2-2 in a tight opening day encounter. Allscott Heath followed up their opening draw with another 2-2 result midweek against Cheadle Heath again, showing they're building something competitive early on.

Telford Town had a nightmare start, losing 6-0 to New Mills on the opening day, and have since picked things up slightly with their women's side thrashing Bilston Town Ladies 8-1. The men's team also lost their first home game heavily to Crewe, who despite that 3-0 defeat against Wolverhampton Casuals in their league debut, showed enough to suggest they won't be pushovers despite their drop from higher levels.

On the squad front, Eccleshall have made early moves by signing defender Phil McKerdy from Wolverhampton Casuals, bringing defensive leadership to the backline. Crewe have added Brazilian centre-back Juliano Silva to bolster their defence. Market Drayton Town signed midfielder Aidan McCann and borrowed centre-half George Handley from Shifnal Town, while Allscott Heath have brought back multiple familiar faces including Harry Morris, who scored on his return, and George Cross, who had been prolific at step level locally.
